item.title: 8-year-old dies and 3 other children admitted in hospital following separate road accidents
item.description: An 8-year-old has died while three remain in Hospital following separate road accidents in Vakabalea in Navua, Adi Davila Road in Nakasi and in Narewa Road in Nadi. Police say the 8-year-old was standing in the middle of the road trying to cross to the other side when he was hit by a vehicle driven by a 32-year-old man on Tuesday.
item.content:encoded:
An 8-year-old has died while three remain in Hospital following separate road accidents in Vakabalea in Navua, Adi Davila Road in Nakasi and in Narewa Road in Nadi.

Police say the 8-year-old was standing in the middle of the road trying to cross to the other side when he was hit by a vehicle driven by a 32-year-old man on Tuesday.

They say the victim was rushed to the Navua Hospital where he was pronounced dead.

They say the suspect will be questioned soon as investigations continue.

In another accident, Police say two children aged 8 and 9 were hit by a vehicle driven by a 42-year-old man along Adi Davila Road in Nakasi, yesterday afternoon.

They say the two victims had suddenly crossed from in front of a parked bus, resulting in the accident.

Both are currently admitted at the CWM Hospital.

In the third accident, a 9-year-old girl was hit by a vehicle driven by a 52-year-old man along Narewa Road yesterday afternoon.

Police say the victim is alleged to have suddenly crossed the road, resulting in the accident.

They say the child is admitted at the Lautoka Aspen Hospital in stable condition.

Assistant Commissioner of Police Operations Kasiano Vusonilawe is calling on parents, guardians, drivers and communities to work together in making our roads safe for children.

ACP Vusonilawe says as we head into the school holidays and busy weeks where large gatherings are expected to take place across the country, the Fiji Police Force is urging everyone to be alert to the movement of children on our roads.

He urges parents and guardians to closely monitor the movement of their children and continue to reinforce the importance of road safety.

item.title: Conjoined twins mother hopeful her babies will live a normal life after surgery
item.description: The mother of conjoined twins, Akeneta Rokobati Tacaqe says she is very happy and excited knowing her babies will be able to live a normal life after the life-changing surgery. item.content:encoded:
The mother of conjoined twins, Akeneta Rokobati Tacaqe says she is very happy and excited knowing her babies will be able to live a normal life after the life-changing surgery.

Speaking to fijivillage News, Mother of twins Di Cecea and Jesipeli Kikau, says the family is currently in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, where the twins are undergoing a one-month period of observation before their life-changing surgery.

Tacaqe says both babies are doing well and are currently under observation by doctors.

She says the doctors in Riyadh have been very helpful.

Tacaqe says doctors from Fiji’s Paediatric Department were the ones who informed the family that surgery could be provided in Riyadh.

She says her family and friends in Fiji have also been very supportive.

Tacaqe says her workmates at the Fiji Meat Industry Board organised a fundraiser, while both her family and her husband’s family also held fundraisers to help with preparations for the family’s trip to Riyadh.

Tacaqe expresses her gratitude to the people in Fiji who have been praying for the babies and asks them to continue praying for the twins thanking everyone for their love and support.

The twins will remain under observation for the one-month period as their family prepares for the next stage of their medical journey in Riyadh.

item.title: Father questions delayed CT scan as Health Minister points to hospital space constraints

item.content:encoded:
The father of a 17-year-old boy is still waiting for his son to receive further medical assessment after he was unable to be transferred from Nadi Hospital to Lautoka Hospital for a CT scan, with Health Minister Dr Ratu Atonio Lalabalavu saying the issue is not a shortage of beds, but a shortage of hospital space.

Speaking to fijivillage News, Mohammed Kalam says his son was admitted to Nadi Hospital at around 5pm last Friday after he began bleeding from the nose and feeling weak.

Kalam says doctors planned to transfer his son to Lautoka Hospital for a CT scan, but the family was later informed that there was no available bed.

He says they were told the transfer would take place on Sunday, but no bed became available, and the family eventually took their son home.

Kalam says they have still not received an update on when his son will be able to receive the required medical assessment.

He is questioning why there are not enough hospital beds to accommodate patients requiring specialised care.

Responding to questions from fijivillage News, Dr Lalabalavu says Fiji has hospital beds available, but the lack of physical space limits how many beds can be accommodated.

He says hospitals can only fit a certain number of beds within their allocated space.

Dr Lalabalavu says the Ministry of Health is working on a replacement and improvement programme.

He says Nadi Hospital now has a new ultrasound scan machine, while an existing X-ray table-mounted machine is also available.

However, Kalam's concern remains focused not only on his son's delayed access to further medical assessment and the CT scan, but also on other patients who may face similar challenges.

fijivillage News is continuing to follow up on the case and the availability of hospital beds and specialised services for patients requiring further assessment.

item.title: Rewa Street and Flagstaff drug accused indicate they will remain silent
item.description: Josua Ravula, Ginna Choi, Peniasi Delai, Yu Yang Feng, Minghui Dai and Zhou Lan have indicated that they will remain silent in the Rewa Street and Flagstaff drug case. This is after Suva Magistrate Sufia Hamza ruled that the six have a case to answer .
item.content:encoded:
Josua Ravula, Ginna Choi, Peniasi Delai, Yu Yang Feng, Minghui Dai and Zhou Lan have indicated that they will remain silent in the Rewa Street and Flagstaff drug case.

This is after Suva Magistrate Sufia Hamza ruled that the six have a case to answer .

Lawyer for the Chinese nationals, Shirley Tivao told the court that her clients have indicated that they will remain silent, but for proper procedure, the translator needs to explain their rights to them.

Lawyer for Choi and Delai, Jerry Dinati says he needs proper instructions from his clients regarding their decision to remain silent, calling evidence and proceeding with him as their lawyer.

The matter has been adjourned to next Thursday.

It is alleged that Josua Ravula was found with unlawful possession of 42.295 grams of methamphetamine.

Yu Yang Feng, Minghui Dai and Zhou Lan are each charged with one count of unlawful possession of illicit drugs for allegedly being found with 39.509 grams of methamphetamine.

Lan is also charged with possession of property suspected to be proceeds of a crime for allegedly being found with FJD$7,180, USD$60, 1,520 in Hong Kong currency and 1,600 Chinese yuan.

Feng is also charged with unlawful supply of illicit drugs. It is alleged that on the 23rd of September, 2025, without lawful authority, Feng engaged in dealings with other persons for the transport and supply of methamphetamine.

He is also charged with being in possession of property suspected to be proceeds of a crime.

Feng was allegedly found with $906.25 in cash. Choi and Peniasi Delai are charged with one count of unlawful possession of illicit drugs for allegedly being found with 0.345 grams of methamphetamine.
